substeps.caption: An example run in the lab as set up: two Kardex Shuttles with every tray loaded (A-O), the floor machines, one MiR250 + UR10e docked at Shuttle 1's opening and the other on its charger. The multi-doser doses 25 mg of an atomized powder and the CubXL adds electrolyte to it, DAL's powder reactivity test (PR #180, cubxl-setup.md §8: 10-50 mg of each atomizer run's powder; the metal it gives up tracks its oxide).

Module 6 (green) holds atomized AlSi10Mg from a rePowder run, its 20-63 µm cut. With our dose post empty, the carousel indexes the module to the station (8 chain links a module) and two P16s lift the electronics carriage on its bar to dock it; it tilts 30°, cap end up, which takes the carriage clear of the post (it parks right over it).

Our shield's door slides open and the shuttle carries the vial in over the post and drops it into the nest: a 4 mm ring round its foot holds it, and the fork goes on down the nest's grooves and backs out. The door shuts; nothing else touches the balance. The vial's rim is 50 mm under the auger's exit (156 mm before).

v5's dose-to doses by weight: a quarter auger turn, then a reading over RS-232, until the HR-202i reads 25 mg (readings illustrative): a heap 6 mm across, drawn to scale, from a 50 mm fall inside the shield. Then one turn back with the vial still under the exit, and the reading settles with the door shut.

The CubXL's own P20 (1-20 µL) takes a 20 µL tip, the capper lifts the seawater cap, and 10 transfers of 20 µL put 200 µL on the powder, 0.4 mm deep (to scale). The copper deck's chloride stock is seawater; DAL's §8 names 0.6 M NaCl.
